equity_bridge.item: Brazil (Yoki/Kitano) sale proceeds received after the Aug-2026 balance date
equity_bridge.note: Closed 2026-09-02 at a base price of R$800m (~US$145m at ~5.5 BRL/USD), before completion adjustments; held at 140 for rounding/adjustments. The 1,031.8 valuation loss was booked in FY2026, so the asset is at realisable value and the 503.0 'liabilities held for sale' leave with it. Not on the 30-Aug-2026 balance sheet used for net debt.

historical_growth.eps_note: GAAP FY2026 EPS is -0.16, so CAGRs are on ADJUSTED diluted EPS: FY2021 3.79, FY2023 4.31, FY2026 3.55 (1,912.0 / 538.5). GAAP-based CAGRs are undefined.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path average over FY2028-FY2036 (management's long-term algorithm of 2-3% organic growth, haircut for four consecutive years of negative organic volume); the equity CAGR is not usable as a growth proxy -- see warning
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-11.7% 3yr) diverges from revenue (-2.9%) by far more than 30pp. Book equity fell from 10,700 to 7,381 because of 3.6bn of debt-funded buybacks over FY2024-FY2026 plus the 1.8bn FY2026 impairments; it measures capital returned and written off, not earning power. Owner-FCF CAGR (-7.9% 3yr) is the relevant series and is essentially identical to reported FCF CAGR (-8.0%): SBC is only 0.4% of revenue, so the decline is cash, not comp -- revenue down 8% over three years with adjusted operating margin compressing from 17.4% to 15.3%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series used for CAGRs: FY2021 2,362.5 (2,452.4 - 89.9), FY2023 1,977.4 (2,089.1 - 111.7), FY2026 1,546.9 (1,626.3 - 79.4). Interest income is not stripped in any year (net debt throughout).

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 is the trough management has guided to: organic sales roughly flat, adjusted operating profit down 8-13% on the 53rd-week lap, incentive-comp normalisation and the yogurt/Brazil exits, adjusted EPS $3.00-3.20 with ~95% FCF conversion. From FY2028 the $3bn cost program (HMM productivity ~4% of COGS plus the supply-chain redesign) offsets 4-5% input inflation and the price investments already made, and EBITDA margin drifts back to the FY2026 adjusted level (18.5%) by FY2032 -- no return to the 20% of FY2025. Revenue grows 1-2%: Pet (Whitebridge, Blue Buffalo fresh formats) and International (Haagen-Dazs, Old El Paso) grow low-to-mid single digits while North America Retail continues to leak volume to private label and GLP-1-dampened categories. Walmart stays at ~22% of sales on existing terms. The dividend is covered (~85% of owner FCF) and buybacks stay paused until leverage falls below ~3.5x.
scenario_narratives.bull: The protein/fibre renovation (Cheerios Protein, Nature Valley protein bars) and the completed price investments stabilise North America Retail volumes by FY2028; Pet re-accelerates to mid-single digits and the sharpened International portfolio compounds at ~5%. The savings program drops through rather than being reinvested, so adjusted EBITDA margin recovers to the FY2025 level (20.5%) by FY2032 and the incoming CEO (McNabb, Jan 2027) holds the long-term algorithm of mid-single-digit profit growth. Exit multiple 18x unlevered FCF (~11x EBITDA) is still below the sector's pre-2023 average, so this case requires only a return to 'normal' staples valuation, not a re-rating.
scenario_narratives.bear: The volume decline is structural rather than cyclical: GLP-1 adoption and the shift to value and private label keep North America Retail organic sales negative through FY2030, Foodservice follows the away-from-home cycle down, and Pet's growth stalls after the $1.5bn goodwill write-down signalled lowered expectations. Savings are consumed by promotional reinvestment and fixed-cost deleverage across 41 plants, pushing EBITDA margin to 15.5%. Further impairments on Blue Buffalo and Progresso follow. With net debt at ~4x EBITDA the dividend is held but not grown and the share count stays flat with no buyback support; the market caps a shrinking staple at 14x unlevered FCF (~9x EBITDA).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value General Mills as a mature, levered, defensive cash generator whose FY2026 GAAP loss is accounting rather than cash: the flows are built from the company's own adjusted operating profit (2,811.5, 15.3%) plus D&A, not from GAAP net income, and the one-off items are reconciled line by line in inputs.notes. Three things decide the answer: (1) whether the FY2027 guided trough is the bottom or a step on the way down (the growth and margin paths); (2) the exit multiple, which is capped at roughly today's EV/EBITDA so no multiple expansion is assumed; and (3) the 13.2bn of net debt, which turns a ~10% swing in enterprise value into a ~25% swing in equity value. SBC is immaterial (0.4% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow and the share count is held flat.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage amplification: net debt is ~55% of the base-case enterprise value, so every 1pt of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly $4/share
Terminal multiple: the cap binds in every scenario; a market that pays 9x rather than 10.5x EBITDA for a shrinking staple takes ~$6/share off the base
FY2027 guidance is only reaffirmed, not de-risked -- Q1 organic was flat, but Q2-Q4 carry the Brazil and 53rd-week laps and the input-inflation peak
Walmart at 22% of sales: a terms reset or shelf-space loss is not in any scenario path explicitly
Further non-cash impairments (Blue Buffalo, Progresso) would not change the flows but would signal the bear path and could pressure covenants/ratings

WACC is set above the mechanical CAPM figure (7.0% vs ~5.7%); at 6% the base case is roughly $9/share higher, so the valuation is conservative on the discount rate and the sensitivity grid shows the range

The flat share count is funded historically but the repurchaser has paused; dividends (1,315.3 in FY2026, $2.44/share) absorb ~85% of owner FCF.
inputs.share_count_basis: 534,687,144 shares outstanding at 2026-09-16 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q cover, line 807-810) plus the 0.5M Q1 FY2027 dilutive increment (diluted 537.9 vs basic 537.4 weighted average, 10-Q:1781-1785) = 535.2M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated the following Sunday, no after-hours print involved
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Q1 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 30 Aug 2026): cash 433.1; current LTD 1,046.8 + notes payable 201.6 + long-term debt 12,367.2 = total debt 13,615.6; net debt 13,182.5. Noncontrolling interests 13.4 -- immaterial, not deducted. Liabilities held for sale 503.0 relate to the Brazil business sold 2026-09-02 (after balance date); see equity_bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. CAPM: 10-yr UST ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.55 gives cost of equity ~7.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% on recent issuance (3.9% after tax); market weights ~58% equity / 42% debt give a mechanical WACC of ~5.7%. 7.0% is used instead: a packaged-food business with net debt/adjusted EBITDA of ~3.9x and four years of negative organic volume should not be capitalised at a rate that assumes the historical beta still holds. 7.0% is applied to all three scenarios -- outcome risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (138.5 in FY2026, 10-K:7602) is expensed inside cost of sales/SG&A, so it is already inside the EBITDA margin paths. Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. No separate lease_cost_pct_path needed; charging one would double-count.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are 13.4 on the Aug-2026 balance sheet with 1.1 of Q1 earnings attributable -- below rounding of the per-share value; not deducted. (The large GMC redeemable interest was retired in FY2022.)
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, consumer'); the adaptations file was consulted for leases/NCI and neither needs an adjustment here. First valuation of this ticker. EARNINGS BASE: FY2026 GAAP results (operating profit 885.8, net loss 85.3, diluted EPS -0.16) are dominated by non-cash items -- a 1,500.0 North America Pet goodwill impairment plus 302.9 of brand-intangible impairments (1,802.9 total), a 1,031.8 valuation loss on the Brazil disposal group, offset by a 1,049.4 divestiture gain on US yogurt, plus 155.5 of restructuring. The company's own reconciliation (10-K:5842-5866) gives ADJUSTED operating profit of 2,811.5 (15.3% margin) vs 3,352.6 (17.2%) in FY2025; adding D&A 555.2 gives adjusted EBITDA 3,366.7 = 18.3% of 18,424.6 revenue, which is the margin anchor for the paths below. The flows are built from that normalized margin, never from GAAP net income; reported FCF 1,626.3 (OCF 2,166.2 less capex 539.9) was unaffected by the impairments because they are non-cash, so last_fcf = 1,626.3 - 79.4 SBC = 1,546.9 (85% conversion of adjusted net earnings 1,912.0). INTEREST INCOME not stripped: 31.0 of interest income sits against 13.6bn of debt; there is no net cash pile being added to EV, so there is nothing to double-count. CASH TAX: adjusted effective tax rate 21.1% FY2026, 20.6% FY2025; cash taxes paid 390.9 ran below the provision in FY2026 (divestiture timing) -- the 21% provision rate is modelled as the sustainable cash rate on EBIT. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture 0 -- GIS runs negative trade working capital (payables 3,715 vs receivables 1,775 + inventory 2,163), and at +/-2% revenue growth the swing is under 1% of FCF either way. HORIZON: 10 years so that the FY2027 guidance trough and the FY2027-FY2030 $3bn savings program both resolve before the terminal year; margins are flat from year 6. TERMINAL CAP: 17x unlevered FCF in the base equals roughly 10.5x EBITDA, i.e. today's depressed EV/EBITDA -- the model assumes no multiple expansion from here; bear 14x, bull 18x (still below the ~12-13x EBITDA the sector averaged pre-2023). Gordon exceeds the cap in all three scenarios, so the cap binds everywhere.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 (Y1) -4.5% reported: organic at the -0.5% guidance midpoint, less ~1.8pts lapping the FY2026 53rd week, ~2pts of Brazil for the nine months after the 2 Sept 2026 sale, and the yogurt tail (Q1 FY2027 printed -3% on flat organic). FY2028+ recovers to 1.0/1.5/2.0% -- the low end of the 2-3% long-term algorithm, reflecting that NA Retail (57% of sales) is still shrinking while Pet and International grow.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 17.3% EBITDA = adjusted operating profit at the guidance midpoint (-10.5% from 2,811.5 = ~2,516, 14.3% of 17,595) plus 3.0% D&A. Recovery to 18.5% by FY2032 returns the business only to its FY2026 adjusted level (18.3%), not to FY2025's 20.0%: the $3bn savings program (~$750m FY2027) is assumed to offset 4-5% input inflation and continued price/brand investment with only a small net gain.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: organic volume has been negative for four consecutive years, FY2027 guidance sits below the company's own long-term algorithm, management itself wrote down $1.8bn of goodwill and brands in FY2026 and flagged Blue Buffalo and Progresso as having thin headroom, and 22% customer concentration in Walmart plus ~3.9x net debt/EBITDA leave little room to absorb a further volume step-down. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- a NA Retail volume inflection, savings dropping through rather than being reinvested, and Pet re-accelerating -- under a new CEO. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
